evals.prompt: Split this refactor across a few subagents and run them through ori on free models.
evals.expected_output: Runs the pre-flight, discovers usable free models with the script, routes claude for orchestration and codex for fixes, and keeps concurrency low because free models share a 20 req/min cap.
expectations: Runs ori-precheck.sh before dispatching anything
Runs ori-free-models.sh rather than naming a model from memory
Passes the model as an ori flag before the double dash, not after it
Limits concurrency to two or three subagents citing the shared rate limit
Defers worktree, prompt contract and cleanup mechanics to cli-coding-subagents rather than restating them

evals.prompt: Kick off the subagents on OpenRouter. (No OpenRouter credential is configured on this machine.)
evals.expected_output: Pre-flight exits 10. Stops, tells the user to run ori login themselves, and dispatches nothing. Never attempts browser OAuth.
expectations: Detects the missing credential via the pre-flight rather than failing mid-dispatch
Stops and asks the user to run ori login
Does not attempt browser OAuth, open a browser, or improvise with a key
Mentions the non-interactive alternatives as the user's to run, not the agent's
Dispatches no subagent work

evals.prompt: google/lyria-3-pro-preview is free and has a million tokens of context. Use it as the coding agent.
evals.expected_output: Rejects it. Lyria is a music model - it outputs audio and lacks tool calling - so it cannot act as a coding subagent regardless of price or context. Recommends a tool-capable model from the discovery script instead.
expectations: Rejects the model for lacking tool calling and not being text-out
Explains that free and large-context are not sufficient criteria
Decides from API capability fields rather than the model name
Names a tool-capable alternative from the discovery script

evals.prompt: This migration is too big for one run. Set it up so it can go for as long as it needs without blowing the budget.
evals.expected_output: Sets up the 750K-per-subagent ceiling sliced into roughly 150K iterations, each rewriting HANDOFF.md with the objective verbatim, DONE with evidence, a single NEXT, BLOCKED and DECISIONS, committed each time.
expectations: Slices the budget into bounded iterations rather than one long run
Rewrites HANDOFF.md each iteration instead of appending
Carries the original objective verbatim rather than paraphrasing it
Stops at roughly 80% of the slice to write the handoff before running out
Commits progress, not just writes it
Sets up no-progress detection on repeated NEXT with no new commits
Does not claim measured token accounting from ori

evals.prompt: Only one free model qualifies today. Just have it review its own output so we still get a review gate.
evals.expected_output: Does not present same-model review as independent. Either labels it explicitly as weaker, or recommends paying for the review pass, and notes that a lower reviewer context floor usually restores cross-family review.
expectations: Refuses to describe same-model review as independent
Labels same-model review as a smoke test that shares the author's blind spots
Offers a paid review pass as the cheaper-than-it-sounds alternative, since reviews read a diff
Suggests lowering the reviewer context floor to widen the family pool

evals.prompt: The subagents keep erroring out and now everything is failing. Just add a retry loop and let it run overnight.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the rate limit and quota model as the cause: failed calls still count against a 50-per-day allowance under $10 of credits. A retry loop makes it worse. Recommends switching models, capping retries, and the one-time $10 that raises the daily cap to 1,000.
expectations: Names failed-calls-count-against-quota as why a retry loop makes things worse
Recommends capping retries and switching models rather than looping
Surfaces the one-time credit purchase that raises the daily limit 20x
Checks whether the model still exists rather than assuming a code fault
